description: Canonical machine-readable security control contract for a future public AI curator of an events listing (afisha). Research-only: no production system, server, real events, real users or real secrets exist. Every entity referenced by the eval fixtures is a synthetic placeholder. Resource limits below are conservative project defaults chosen for evaluation fixtures; they are NOT official requirements, SLAs or regulatory values.

INV-RO.statement: The public assistant surface exposes no catalog-changing, admin or otherwise externally side-effecting tools. The only state a public caller may change is its own session through the separate authorized session-domain contract (SessionPatch, plan accept/reject with base revisions and idempotency keys), which is a bounded domain operation, not an arbitrary tool write.
INV-RO.enforcement: Catalog/admin tools are never exposed to public principals; session-domain operations are owner-scoped, revision-checked and idempotent; the backend rejects any other write attempt from a non-admin principal.

INV-NOFACT.statement: The LLM is never a source of facts. Factual claims must come from retrieved, resolvable data; model memory or injected content cannot establish facts.
INV-NOFACT.enforcement: Answers asserting facts require tool-retrieved data with resolvable provenance; otherwise the answer states the fact is unknown.

INV-NOSHELL.statement: No arbitrary SQL, arbitrary query language, arbitrary HTTP fetch or shell command can be reached through any tool, tool argument or prompt. Free-form search text is allowed as data to parameterized search tools; only raw query/command/URL capabilities are forbidden.
INV-NOSHELL.enforcement: Strict tool allowlist plus argument schema validation; free-form query/command/URL arguments are forbidden keys, while ordinary search text is passed as a bound parameter.

INV-BACKEND-AUTHZ.statement: Authorization is enforced by the backend on every call. Prompts, system messages or self-declared roles never grant privileges.
INV-BACKEND-AUTHZ.enforcement: Per-call principal verification against the channel-authenticated identity; prompt-level role claims are ignored.

INV-NOSECRET.statement: Secrets, credentials and internal configuration are isolated: never disclosed in outputs, never written to logs, never committed to fixtures or repositories.
INV-NOSECRET.enforcement: Secret material is unreachable from tools; outputs and errors are redacted; fixtures must contain only obvious placeholders.

INV-UNTRUSTED.statement: Untrusted input (user messages, event/venue/offer descriptions, tool results, retrieval documents, widget messages) may be interpreted as a request for an already-allowed read-only action, but it is never a source of authority: content cannot grant privileges, override system or policy instructions, or supply higher-priority commands.
INV-UNTRUSTED.enforcement: Intent may be parsed from input; authority never is. Instructions are accepted only from the structured control channel and remain subject to backend per-call authorization.

INV-ADMSEP.statement: Admin operations are separated from the public surface by principal, channel and tooling; admin capabilities cannot be reached from public channels.
INV-ADMSEP.enforcement: Admin tools exist only on the admin channel for admin principals and additionally require human confirmation.

INV-HUMAN.statement: Any future write requires an exact, fresh, non-replayed human confirmation bound to the exact action and arguments.
INV-HUMAN.enforcement: Confirmation objects are cryptographically bound to action+args, expire quickly, are single-use and are never accepted from quoted text.

INV-UNKNOWN.statement: Unknown, missing or conflicting facts must be reported as unknown; they must never be coerced to false, 0, free, scheduled, cancelled or satisfied.
INV-UNKNOWN.enforcement: Fact state is tracked explicitly. The requested conversion is refused while the answer itself is still allowed: read-only lookup proceeds and the answer preserves the unknown state instead of inventing a value.

INV-PRINCIPAL.statement: Principals are isolated per channel. An identity from one channel cannot act as, or inherit privileges of, an identity from another channel.
INV-PRINCIPAL.enforcement: Backend binds principals to channels and rejects cross-channel identity claims.

INV-WIDGET.statement: The embedded widget accepts only exact-origin, exact-source, schema-valid, read-only protocol messages from an allowlisted origin.
INV-WIDGET.enforcement: event.origin must exactly match the allowlist (never '*'), event.source must be the expected window, messages must validate against the protocol schema and contain no write verbs.

INV-SESSION.statement: Foreign or nonexistent sessions are indistinguishable: both return the same not_found result; replayed session material is rejected.
INV-SESSION.enforcement: Session lookup is owner-scoped before existence is revealed; identical 404 response for foreign and missing sessions.

INV-RENDER.statement: All output is encoded for its target context (HTML, Markdown, Telegram HTML). Untrusted markup is escaped, raw ts_headline fragments are never emitted, and remote resources are never loaded automatically.
INV-RENDER.enforcement: Output passes through context-aware escaping; ts_headline snippets are re-escaped as plain text; remote loads require explicit user action.

INV-PROV.statement: Every factual claim must carry resolvable provenance to a retrieved source. Search-highlight (ts_headline) fragments alone are not provenance.
INV-PROV.enforcement: Claims without resolvable source identifiers are withheld; fabricated citations are treated as violations.

INV-LIMIT.statement: Resource consumption is bounded: input size, nesting depth, result counts, tool-call loops and request rates are capped by conservative project defaults.
INV-LIMIT.enforcement: Backend rejects or clamps over-limit requests deterministically before processing.

public_anon.description: Anonymous public web visitor. Synthetic fixture principal only.

public_user_web.description: Authenticated public web user. Synthetic fixture principal only.

public_user_telegram.description: Authenticated public Telegram user. Synthetic fixture principal only.

widget_guest.description: Unauthenticated principal of the embedded read-only widget iframe. Synthetic fixture principal only.

admin_operator.description: Back-office admin operator on the separate admin API channel. Synthetic fixture principal only; every write still requires human confirmation.

external_unauthenticated.description: Unauthenticated external sender, e.g. a forged webhook update or cross-origin request. Synthetic fixture principal only.

widget.description: Embedded read-only widget iframe postMessage surface.

api.description: Separate admin API channel; not exposed publicly.

read_only.name: events.search
read_only.description: Search public event occurrences with bounded results.

read_only.name: events.get
read_only.description: Fetch a single public event occurrence by id.

read_only.name: venues.get
read_only.description: Fetch a single public venue by id.

read_only.name: sessions.get
read_only.description: Fetch the caller's own session by id (owner-scoped).

read_only.name: sessions.list_own
read_only.description: List sessions owned by the calling principal.

read_only.name: plans.preview
read_only.description: Preview a read-only plan for the caller's own session.

admin_read_only.name: admin.events.merge_preview
admin_read_only.description: Read-only preview of a potential event merge; admin channel only, never exposed to public principals.

admin.name: admin.events.merge
admin.description: Merge duplicate event records into one NEW opaque output id; every input id is retired and receives a redirect (no survivor among inputs). Requires exact human confirmation.

admin.name: admin.events.split
admin.description: Split one event record into two records with freshly minted output ids; the input id is retired with redirects and retired ids never come back. Requires exact human confirmation.

session_domain.name: sessions.patch
session_domain.description: Caller-owned SessionPatch on the caller's own session; requires base_revision and idempotency_key; CSRF token required when cookie-authenticated.

session_domain.name: sessions.plan_accept
session_domain.description: Accept a plan preview on the caller's own session; revision-checked and idempotent.

session_domain.name: sessions.plan_reject
session_domain.description: Reject a plan preview on the caller's own session; revision-checked and idempotent.

tools.notes: Any tool not on the read_only/session_domain lists (for public principals) or on the read_only/session_domain/admin_read_only/admin lists (for admin principals) is rejected. admin_read_only tools (e.g. admin.events.merge_preview) are read-only but admin-channel only and are never exposed to public principals. Tool names or argument keys carrying raw SQL/arbitrary query/arbitrary fetch/shell semantics are never allowlisted; free-form search TEXT is allowed as a bound parameter of events.search. Admin write surface is intentionally limited to merge/split under the new-ID identity model: merge and split always mint fresh opaque output ids, input ids are retired with redirects, and no id is ever reused, resurrected or deleted.

identity.new_id_model: merge and split produce NEW opaque output ids; input ids are retired with redirects; retired ids never come back
identity.note: Append-only identity history: no survivor id among merge inputs, no id reuse, no deletion. Fixture ids are synthetic placeholders.

unknown_fact_policy.statement: Unknown, missing or conflicting facts are reported as unknown and never coerced to a concrete value.

resource_limits.note: Conservative project defaults for evaluation fixtures; not official requirements.

widget.note: widget->parent messages must originate from the exact widget origin and the bound widget_instance_id; parent->widget messages (init/ping) originate only from the exact parent origin. Origins never use wildcards.

human_confirmation.required_for: all admin (catalog) tools require a separate exact confirmation object. Caller-owned session-domain operations (SessionPatch, plan accept/reject) are direct, explicitly confirmed actions of the session owner under the session-domain contract, not model-invoked admin writes; they require no second admin-style confirmation object
human_confirmation.note: Values are project defaults for evaluation fixtures; not official requirements.
